It's been another excellent year for gaming with new hardware, accessories and so many essential new games that playing them all is practically impossible. If you're not immersed in the world of gaming, knowing what the best gaming gifts are can be extremely overwhelming.

That's why I've done the research for you. I'm one of Tom's Guide's gaming experts, and I've picked out a selection of gifts that any gamer would love to receive this year. I've got options with a range of prices, from affordable picks to premium products, with each broken down in simple categories.

Whether the gamer in your life plays on PC, PlayStation, Nintendo, Xbox or mobile, these are the best gaming gifts in 2026.

Looking for more gift inspiration? Check out our guide to the best holiday gifts.

Choose to follow your gaming destiny with the powerful Victus Gaming Laptop leading you to immersive, fun-filled experiences. Enjoy playing with great, stable performance with an Intel Core processor and NVIDIA GeForce RTX Laptop GPU. OMEN Gaming Hub's performance toolkit elevates play with software enhancements and personalized hardware control.

The Xbox Series X remains the pinnacle of Microsoft's console family. It's a powerful, chunky black box that can run the latest games at 4K resolution at 60 frames per second without breaking a sweat. Plus, Xbox Game Pass is the best subscription service in gaming. It also offers the most robust backwards compatibility features of any console, letting you experience classic games from every Xbox generation.

Thanks to unwelcome price hikes, the Xbox Series S isn't quite the budget-friendly machine it was once. Nevertheless, it's still the cheapest current-generation console on the market. It plays all the same games as its more powerful Xbox Series X sibling, but with some graphical sacrifices. It's a great pick if you don't want to spend eyewatering sums on a console, and is the cheapest way to play Grand Theft Auto VI in 2026 — which is an especially big selling point.

A second controller is always useful for co-op gaming on Xbox consoles. You could get the standard black or white model, but the Forza Horizon 6 Limited Edition is way snazzier. Released in conjunction with the latest Forza game, its neon-bright yellow/pink/blue color scheme celebrates the title's vast open-world map of Japan. It also features translucent plastic, which is clearly back in style in 2026.

The latest title in the Gears of War franchise is a prequel set during Emergence Day (aka E-Day), the fateful moment when the Locust hordes first attacked humanity. You play as series stalwart Marcus Fenix alongside his best buddy, Dom Santiago, and a new crew of COG soldiers battling on the front lines of this future war. In TG's Gears of War E-Day review, we gave it an 'Editor's Choice' award, calling it "the must-own Xbox exclusive of 2026."

If the gamer in your life hasn't already picked up Grand Theft Auto VI, then they're probably asking for it for Christmas. It's the long-awaited return of the GTA franchise after 13 years. This blockbuster is set in Vice City and introduces the franchise's first playable female protagonist in the story mode. Note: this is a "code in box" edition; it doesn't come with a physical game disc.

The PS5/PS5 Slim is the best-selling console of this generation and, in 2026, continues to make an excellent case for itself. Its library is overflowing with great games, many in 4K resolution at 60 frames per second. Its DualSense controller is packed with novel features, like haptic feedback and adaptive triggers. Plus, PlayStation is proudly boasting that "PS5 is the best place to play" GTA 6. There's also the PS5 Pro, for those demanding the most powerful console, but finding the already pricey Pro in stock is very difficult at present.

Sony's latest official PlayStation headset is the PlayStation Pulse, not to be confused with the PlayStation Pulse 3D, which arrived back in November 2020 alongside the PS5 console. It's a slick wireless headset with a built-in microphone and full UI integration on PS5. Its look also mirrors the PS5's two-tone aesthetics, so it's a great buy for gamers who want their entertainment setup to match.

The DualSense controller is great, but if you want a proper "pro" pad, the Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited is designed to give competitive gamers an edge. Its biggest upgrade is the built-in display, which lets you customize any of its seven shortcuts on the fly, and it also sports TMR joysticks, dual-mode actuation triggers, and a docking station for easy charging. It's also compatible with PC.

PS5's big blockbuster exclusive for 2026 is Marvel's Wolverine, the latest superhero romp from Spider-Man developer Insomniac Games. It's quite repetitive, but it's essentially a playable summer blockbuster that does have its appeal. Just be aware, it's not one for younger gamers. Wolverine's claws are used for all manner of violence. Trust me, Wolverine earns its "M" rating.

Grand Theft Auto VI is not just the biggest game of 2026, but the most anticipated game of the whole decade. Sony and Rockstar have confirmed it'll "play best on PlayStation," making the PS5 the place to experience this open-world crime epic 13 years in the making. As with the Xbox version, this is a "code in box" edition, without a physical disc, but it gives you the full game, and an actual box is nicer to wrap than some digital store vouchers.

The Nintendo Switch 2 was recently voted the console you should buy in 2026 by the Tom's Guide staff, and it's not hard to see why. Like its predecessor, it's a hybrid system, letting you play on a TV or undock for portable play on its 7.9-inch LCD display. Now in its second year, the Switch 2's library has really swelled in size, which makes deciding what to play first quite a challenge.

The Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller is a must-have extra if you plan to use your Switch 2 in TV Mode for extended periods. It's the best Switch 2 controller around, offering a traditional button layout, ludicrously long battery life, and even comes with two back buttons. The Joy-Con 2 controllers work well for portable play, but if your Switch 2 is docked, you'll want to play on a Pro pad.

The Nintendo Switch 2's internal storage fills up very fast, with some games requiring more than 50 GB to install. For a portable system, this is a major pain, as you don't want to be deleting and redownloading software all the time. Fortunately, this Samsung 256GB microSD Express Card gives the Switch 2 plenty of additional storage, and comes sporting a charming little Mario design.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has been remade for the Nintendo Switch 2, and in a word, it's stunning. This complete remake of the classic Nintendo 64 offers overhauled visuals, improved controls, and a few smart tweaks to make the timeless game even more modern. Ocarina of Time was considered a masterpiece back in 1998, and this new version on Switch 2 has earned the same plaudits.

If you want a Switch 2 game that the whole family can play this holiday season, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is my top pick. It's a part of the spiritual successor series to Wii Sports, offering a large collection of sports mini-games that use motion controls to mimic the real thing. It's approachable even for non-gamers, and is sure to delight players of all ages. Just don't blame me if it causes a few overly competitive rounds of virtual bowling.

Upgrade your mobile gaming with the excellent Backbone Pro controller. It turns your smartphone into a device resembling the Nintendo Switch 2, giving you greater control of your mobile gaming experience and saving you from trying to play AAA games on a touchscreen. It's super portable, and with 40 hours of battery, the Backbone Pro will always have juice when you need it.

Xbox celebrated its 25th Anniversary this year, leading to a slew of limited edition products; one of my favorites is this GameSir X5 Lite mobile controller. It's an officially licensed accessory that, just like the Backbone Pro, turns your smartphone into a proper portable gaming device. It comes decked out in an attractive colorway that's a nod to the classic Xbox green. Its more wallet-friendly price means some compromises, but it's a capable, cheaper pick compared to the Backbone Pro.

The Steam Deck OLED lags behind its competition when it comes to internal components, but it's still among the finest portable gaming devices around. It's great for tearing through your Steam backlog or enjoying the best indie games around; just don't expect to be playing the latest 2026 releases on the Deck. Unfortunately, post-launch price hikes have made this a tougher recommendation. At $789 for the 512GB model, it's overpriced, but its overall quality gets it a nod in this roundup.

If you've got very deep pockets (and can find it in stock), you could make somebody's holiday season by gifting them the cutting-edge Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20. It's an upgrade on the ROG Xbox Ally X, with a stellar OLED display and fantastic ergonomics. However, it's hard to get over the sticker shock of the price. It makes the Steam Deck look affordable, which is really saying something. This is only for a gamer in your life who has been positively saintly in 2026.

The Evercade Nexus is a handheld device designed for those who love retro gaming. It includes a 5.89-inch IPS display, dual analogue sticks, and wireless headphone support. There's no digital store to download games; instead, it's compatible with more than 80 physical Evercade cartridges (that's 700+ games). To get your collection started, the Evercade Nexus comes bundled with the Banjo-Kazooie Double Pack, collecting a pair of classic 3D platformers on a single cartridge. It's a nostalgia gamer's perfect handheld system.

The VR gaming boom never quite exploded. Even PlayStation seems to have given up on the PSVR 2. However, the Meta Quest 3S is still a great, more budget-friendly virtual reality headset. Ideal for a gamer who already has all console/PC hardware they need. It comes bundled with Golf+, a VR game that lets you step onto the green in the most immersive way possible outside of paying for an overinflated membership at your local golf club.

The music rhythm game genre is making a big comeback this year thanks to Stage Tour. Taking inspiration from Guitar Hero and Rock Band, you play along to a setlist of more than 90 tracks either on a regular controller or for the full rockstar experience on a plastic Guitar. This $129 bundle includes the Stage Tour game and a Kramer Wireless Guitar Controller and is available on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC.

Lego has released a few gaming-themed sets this year, and while the Lego PlayStation 1 is very novel, my pick of the bunch is the Lego Donkey Kong Arcade machine, which recreates a classic arcade cabinet playing the game that introduced the world to Mario. It looks great on display and comes with a play feature that lets you simulate the game in motion, with Mario jumping over barrels.

#3272. Tyra Banks Taps Andy Vallentine To Direct Sally Hansen Film

EXCLUSIVE: Tyra Banks’ Smize Productions has tapped Andy Vallentine (The Mattachine Family) to direct its Sally Hansen feature film, which Deadline announced was in development last year.

In addition to his directing work for Hollywood, Vallentine has a background creating visually bold work for major beauty brands including Sephora and MAC Cosmetics, touts a release from SMiZE Productions. His experience fits into the Sally Hansen world of vintage Hollywood glamour, beauty, fashion and color.

The film, as yet untitled, follows a team determined to uncover the real Sally Hansen — chasing clues, rumors and myths — while juxtaposing her untold story against today’s global nail obsession. Blending beauty with business intrigue, the film explores how Hansen built one of the industry’s most enduring empires decades before “beauty influencer” was even a phrase — and how her legacy still shapes the $50 billion nail market. Watch on Deadline

“I’ve always been drawn to tenacious, impossible stories. Sally Hansen built a beauty empire, and like so many women before and after her, she was nearly written out of history anyway,” Vallentine said. “I’ve spent my career directing campaigns for beauty brands like Sephora and MAC, and now I can’t wait to turn the camera around to tell her unbelievable story and the real-life search to find her.”

Added Banks, “Andy has this incredible visual imagination and a deep understanding of storytelling, plus a real connection to the beauty world, to bring all of that to life. I want people to know Sally the woman, not just Sally the bottle.”

Smize Productions’ global slate includes scripted, unscripted, live theater and ice-cream-themed entertainment projects in the U.S., Canada and Australia, with additional announcements slated through 2026.

Vallentine is repped by Heroes and Villains.

#3271. iOS 27.3 adds Siri AI usage limits, here’s what counts toward your limit

Earlier this week, Apple revealed that Siri AI usage limits will be implemented in iOS 27.3 and explained how iCloud+ increases those limits. Now we have a real-world example of what it looks like when limits are hit, and details on what counts toward those limits.

Siri AI and select other AI features will begin having usage limits in iOS 27.3 for advanced tasks.

This is standard practice with other AI services like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude because these tools rely on server-based models rather than running entirely on-device.

Here’s an example from the iOS 27.3 beta showing what it looks like when you hit your Siri AI daily usage limit. Per Ben in a post on X:

I hit my Siri AI usage limit, it still works though, including complex questions pic.twitter.com/XYYNPMnSnn

In a follow-up post, Ben clarifies that complex questions did stop working shortly after posting. As expected though, basic requests continued to work as usual—they don’t have a usage limit.

One question that Apple hasn’t made clear is what qualifies as a complex or “advanced” Siri AI request. The company shares just two examples of something advanced:

Suppose it gets it wrong like it does most of the time. I wonder if that still counts.

But leaker pdfu has discovered exactly the instructions Siri AI follows to determine whether a request counts as basic or advanced. In a post on X he outlines the parameters for requests deemed “advanced.”

Siri AI will check the request against this list, and if it involves any of these, it’s deemed “advanced.”

It would be helpful if Apple publicly documented these guidelines for users. But perhaps after iOS 27.3 ships and usage limits are fully implemented, we’ll get more detail from the company.

What do you think of Siri AI’s parameters for advanced requests in iOS 27.3? Let us know in the comments.

#3270. These Noise-Canceling Skullcandy Headphones Are 50% Off Ahead of Black Friday

Black Friday is an excellent time to score a new pair of headphones that would otherwise be a splurge, with retailers like Amazon and Walmart already offering massive discounts on tech essentials from top brands a week ahead of the holiday. One of the early Black Friday deals that should be on your radar is the Skullcandy Crusher ANC 2 headphones, a mid-range noise-canceling option that’s perfect for bass lovers and is currently 50% off, dropping to $119.99 (originally $239.99).

PCMag says they deliver “brain-rattling levels of bass” and have a comfortable fit, with generous memory foam cushioning and minimal clamping pressure that lends itself well to long listening sessions. The aesthetic is nothing to scoff at either, with a refined and modern style. It’s worth noting they also come in a hardshell zip-up case with a fabric-lined exterior.

Powered by 40mm dynamic drivers, they offer reliable noise cancellation with the ANC slider set to max on the companion app, which lets users adjust a range of controls and listening modes, including the intensity of bass. Battery life lasts around 50 to 60 hours per charge, with Skullcandy claiming that you get four hours of listening time from around 10 minutes of charging. While brands like Bose will outperform in ANC quality, if you’re looking for noise-canceling audio gear that checks most boxes at a reasonable price point, the Skullcandy Crusher ANC 2 headphones are a smart choice, especially at over $100 off.

AI has come a long way in 2026, and it's no longer something you only use through ChatGPT. This holiday season, some of the most exciting AI features are built right into gadgets you can wrap up and put under the tree.

From sports gear for kids to smart glasses and smart chess boards, these interactive toys bring playtime to life. Best of all, with so many to choose from, there's surely an AI-powered gift for just about everyone on your list.

We've rounded up 11 of the best AI gadgets to give this holiday season, starting at just $99. Whether you're shopping for an energetic, creative or curious kid these gifts offer something beyond another screen or subscription.

StickerboxWhat kid doesn’t love stickers? Well then how about a device that makes stickers based on whatever they ask? That’s the premise behind the Stickerbox, which uses AI to interpret your child’s imagination and turn it into something they can stick onto something in seconds. And, the Stickerbox doesn’t have a camera or collect voice information — all it does is make stickers, simple as that. In our Stickerbox review, our kids absolutely loved it.

HP Victus Gaming LaptopChoose to follow your gaming destiny with the powerful Victus Gaming Laptop leading you to immersive, fun-filled experiences. Enjoy playing with great, stable performance with an Intel Core processor and NVIDIA GeForce RTX Laptop GPU. OMEN Gaming Hub's performance toolkit elevates play with software enhancements and personalized hardware control.

Ball2Ball2 is an interactive, movement-based toy that gets kids off the couch and working together through active, game-style play. It’s ideal for families with multiple children, rainy afternoons and snow days when energy needs an outlet without relying on screens. While it requires a companion app to run, the laughter, movement and cooperative fun it creates make the small inconvenience well worth it.

Dex CameraThis is an AI-powered smart camera designed for kids ages 3 to 8. It turns real-world exploration into active language learning. Instead of locking children to a stationary screen, Dex encourages them to explore their surroundings, point, and take photos. The device instantly identifies objects, speaks their names aloud in one of 16 supported languages, and builds contextual mini-lessons around each discovery.

GoChess Air Smart Chess BoardWhether you're shopping for a chess enthusiast or someone who's just learning the game, GoChess puts an AI-powered spin on a classic favorite. This smart chessboard combines traditional gameplay with modern technology, making it easier than ever to sharpen your skills, challenge friends and enjoy a competitive match.

One of its standout features is its built-in AI coaching, which uses colorful LED lights to provide real-time feedback and suggest moves as you play. It's like having a personal chess instructor sitting beside you, helping you improve without taking the fun out of the game.

With 32 AI difficulty levels, players can challenge themselves against a virtual opponent that matches their abilities. The board also supports online play through Chess.com and Lichess, allowing users to compete against friends and chess enthusiasts around the world.

Miko 3This little AI-powered toy can roll around and interact with your kids, play music, and create challenges and games based on your child’s responses. It also has a 4.7-inch touchscreen with two-way calling, so you can talk to your kid through the Miko app. And, it has a bunch of activities from Disney, Paramount, and Da Vinci kids, ranging from puzzles to coding. Keep in mind you’ll need a subscription ($8.25/month) to get the most out of it.

Curio VoiceThe Curio is a small plush toy that listens, learns and converses with kids. You can choose from three characters — Grok, Gabbo, and Grem — which use cloud-based AI to respond to your child, play music, and tell stories. If the outer plush part gets dirty, you can separate it from the electronics to give it a wash. And, while it needs to be connected to Wi-Fi to work, there’s no subscription. When we reviewed the Curio, our kids were certainly intrigued.

Casio MoflinIf you have a loved one that’s looking for some furry companionship, but is allergic to cats or dogs — or simply can’t take care of them — then the Moflin could be the answer. This little furball uses AI to shape its personality based on how you interact with it — it responds to your voice and being petted and scratched by moving around and making some of the most adorable sounds ever. Check out our Casio Moflin review to see how much we liked it.

StrikeSphere Speed BallThe StrikeSphere Speed Ball was an instant hit with my 12-year-old, largely because it turns every kick into a challenge. A built-in sensor measures each shot and displays a score of up to 999 directly on the ball, so there’s no app or phone required. He immediately started trying to beat his previous score, and that simple competitive element kept him playing far longer than I expected. The ball is a size 4, rather than the regulation size 5 my older son normally uses, which is my biggest complaint. Still, for kids who love competition, it makes ordinary soccer practice much more engaging.

Ray-Ban MetaThe Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses offer many of the features of Meta's camera-equipped smart glasses, minus the camera. You can listen to music and podcasts, take calls, send messages, hear navigation directions and ask Meta AI questions without reaching for your phone. They also support live translation and hands-free voice commands. The lightweight design, comfortable fit and optional Transitions lenses make them easy to wear throughout the day. You won't be taking photos, recording videos or asking AI to identify what you're looking at, but that's the point. These glasses deliver everyday convenience without making everyone around you wonder if they're being recorded.

Huuch Motion BundleThe HUUCH Motion Bundle turns screen time into active play with AI-powered motion tracking that lets kids control games using their bodies instead of traditional controllers. Designed for ages 3 and up, the compact console connects to your TV and supports up to four players. It includes 10 games, with more available through an optional subscription. My three kids had a blast playing together, although setup was frustrating and motion tracking wasn't always reliable. It's a fun option for getting kids moving indoors.

#3267. Patrick Stewart Cause Of Death Revealed

We now have the official cause of death for Sir Patrick Stewart. The star of Star Trek: The Next Generation, Star Trek: Picard, the X-Men film franchise and much more died October 28 from Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia, according to his death certificate obtained by TMZ.

The death certificate also lists cardiopulmonary arrest and a neurocognitive disorder with Lewy body — a progressive form of dementia that affects memory, thinking and movement, according to TMZ. Watch on Deadline

The family statement announcing his death noted that his passing followed “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.” Stewart was 86.

RELATED: 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries

Stewart, whose career spanned nearly six decades, was a three-time Olivier Award winner and a Tony Award nominee for his stage work, including numerous Shakespeare productions. He won a Grammy in 1995 and received multiple Emmy, Golden Globe and SAG Award nominations for his work across television and film.

In 1987 he took on the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation, ensuring his place in TV history and the pop culture landscape. He played the USS Enterprise captain on the popular syndicated drama for seven seasons from 1987-94 and several film installments, beginning with Star Trek: Generations in 1994. He later reprised the role in the global hit Paramount+ series Star Trek: Picard. The series concluded its third and final season in April 2023.

RELATED: ‘Green Room’ Writer/Director Recalls How Patrick Stewart “Saved The Day” When Film Was Almost Axed, Would Tell Fans: “Don’t Root For The Nazis”

Stewart also was praised for his portrayal of Charles Xavier aka Professor X, a role he originated in the 2000 film X-Men and reprised throughout the franchise’s many hit sequels including the hit Logan, opposite Hugh Jackman as Logan/Wolverine. Stewart also reprised the role in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, set for release on December 18, marking his eighth time portraying the character.

Stewart’s many additional screen credits include Coda; L.A. Story; Green Room; Blunt Talk; Robin Hood: Men in Tights; Conspiracy Theory; I, Claudius; Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy; The Kid Who Would Be King; Match; The King of Texas; Jeffrey; Dune and Excalibur. Stewart also did voice work on The Simpsons, Seth MacFarlane’s Family Guy and American Dad! as such films as The Prince of Egypt, Chicken Little and Jimmy Neutron: Boy Genius.

RELATED: Ian McKellen Pays Tribute To Patrick Stewart: “He Wore His Heart On His Sleeve”

#3266. The Best Tech Deals From Costco's Early Black Friday Sale

Sam's Club, Walmart, Amazon, and other retailers have been churning out early Black Friday deals since last week, so if you haven't been paying attention, you've already missed out on some good deals. But all hope is not lost: Costco recently started its own early sale, so you're still in time to find something you want at a low price. Below, I've rounded up my favorite tech deals from their sale—but keep in mind you'll need a membership to take advantage of these deals.

A powerful monitor with high-end specs can make gaming more immersive and greatly reduce input lag, which is helpful for any serious gamer looking for an edge over their opponents. The Samsung Odyssey G9 is a 49-inch gaming monitor with some impressive specs, including a 240Hz refresh rate and a 1 ms response time. It's available for $699.99 (originally $899.99), $200 off and the lowest price it has reached this year.

If you're looking for a more premium (and far more massive) gaming monitor, the 57-inch Samsung Odyssey Neo G9, one of the best ultra-wide gaming monitors on the market, is currently on sale for $1,449.99 ($2,499.99 at launch). This monitor came out in 2023, earning an "excellent" review from PCMag for its impressive 7,680 x 2,160 4K resolution, its great color range and accuracy, a 240Hz refresh rate, 1,000 nits of brightness, and its overall design. To make full use of its powerful 240Hz refresh rate, you'll need to use DisplayPort 2.1, or you'll be limited to 120Hz. You'll also need a powerful graphics card. But if you have the right setup, this thing really delivers.

The 15.3-inch Lenovo Legion is a powerful gaming laptop with premium specs, and with the current $600 discount, it's down to $1999.99 (originally $2,599.99). It has a powerful AMD Ryzen AI 9 processor, 32 GB of RAM, a GeForce RTX 5070 graphics card, and 1TB of SSD. PCMag gave the more affordable 5i version an excellent review for its price and performance, so if you have the cash for it, this one is even better.

A soundbar is a great way to improve a home entertainment system without spending too much money. This 5.1 TCL Q6CH setup is currently $199.99 (originally $299.99), including a soundbar and subwoofer. This soundbar came out in 2024 and supports Dolby Atmos and DTS:X for that 3D sound, as well as AI Sonic, a tool that tunes your sound settings based on the setup of your room.

The latest AirPods Pro are a big step up from their previous generation. The third iteration of Apple's iconic earbuds deliver a number of quality-of-life and software improvements that make them worth the typical premium over the AirPods Pro 2—and right now, the AirPods Pro 3 are even cheaper than the previous generation: They're $179 at Costco (originally $249) in an early Black Friday deal.

The 15-inch MacBook Air is down to $1,249 (originally $1,499), the lowest price since Apple hiked prices this past summer. The M5 MacBook Air is the best laptop for most people looking for a new machine in 2026. In comparison to the already excellent M4 Air, the M5 base model has double the storage, and the powerful M5 chip makes the performance even smoother, according to Mashable's review. The aluminum design is as good as you'd expect from Apple's most popular portable laptop, and it includes a Liquid Retina display, Touch ID, a 12MP Center Stage Camera, and the Magic Keyboard.

The 15.6-inch Acer Aspire Go is a great value at its current $499.99 price (originally $699.99). The display is a touchscreen; it sports an AMD Ryzen 5 processor and it has 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage. These aren't specs you normally find at this price, making it a great laptop for anyone looking to stretch their money as far as possible while getting a workhorse of a laptop.

I'm a fan of TCL TVs, and currently own the "non-pro" version of this TV. The 65-inch QM6K Pro is $599.99 (originally $999.99) and has the same internal hardware and Mini-LED panel as the regular QM6K, but it adds a CrystGlow anti-reflective coating that makes it more viewable in well-lit rooms and helps maintain a high picture contrast. The 144 Hz native refresh rate makes gaming smooth, and support for Dolby Vision IQ, HDR10+, HDR10, and HLG means you're well positioned to get the best sound quality when streaming movies or shows.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

#3264. Jorrybell Agoto Dies: ‘Filipiñana’ Breakout Actress Was 32

Jorrybell Agoto, the star of Rafael Manuel’s award-winning debut feature Filipiñana, died November 17 following a battle with lymphoma, her family said. She was 32.

Epicmedia Productions, the Philippine production company behind Filipiñana, posted on its Instagram account: “We love you, Belle. No more pain.”

Manuel posted: “The tragedy of this loss cannot be put into words. The world has just lost one of its brightest stars. We have just lost a great friend. But our thoughts and prayers go out especially to Jorrybell’s family who have just lost a loving older sister and a devoted daughter.”

Filipiñana premiered at this year’s Sundance Film Festival, where it won the Special Jury Award for Creative Vision in the World Cinema Dramatic Competition. It is also the Philippines’ entry for the Best International Feature category of next year’s Oscars. Watch on Deadline

Agoto played the lead role of a quiet but determined resort worker at a high-end golf club in the film, which explores themes of gentrification, class and globalization. She also starred in the original short film, Filipiñana (2020), that the feature was based on. Also directed by Manuel, the short won a Silver Bear Jury Prize at the Berlinale.

Born on September 25, 1994, in Ilocos, Philippines, Agoto started acting in community theater at a young age before graduating with a BA in Theater Arts from Polytechnic University of the Philippines. She also had roles in short films including Cross My Heart and Hope t Die and such features as Jun Robles Lana’s Sisa, which premiered at the 2025 Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival, and Lawrence Fajardo’s Silenced Nights, which premiered at this year’s Toronto Film Festival.

The Film Development Council of the Philippines also issued a statement following the news of her passing: “The Film Development Council of the Philippines extends its deepest condolences to the family and loved ones of Ms. Jorrybell Agoto — Lead Actress, Filipiñana (1994–2026). Your contribution to the Philippine film industry will remain etched in our hearts. Thank you so much, and farewell, Jorrybell.”

Kino Lorber, which is distributing Filipiñana in the U.S., also remembered the young actress and paid tribute to her talent: “While we never met Jorrybell, we felt like we had through the light she brought to Isabel in Filipiñana. Cinema is poorer for having lost her so young.”

Filipiñana is being released in the UK and Ireland this weekend by BFI Distribution. Kino Lorber released the film in the U.S. in August and is organizing a series of screenings as part of its Oscar campaign.

#3258. How Microcredentials Can Help Engineers Build Trustworthy AI

IEEE Credentialing Program pairs AI governance standards with microcredentials

Kaitlyn Ridel is the IEEE microcredentials marketing specialist.

Engineering teams are moving at breakneck speed to integrate artificial intelligence, but they are running into a formidable new barrier: compliance issues. Translating high-level AI ethics, governance, and auditing into daily operational workflows has become one of the industry’s toughest challenges.

“AI ethics” refers to the principles developers use to govern and operate workflows. “Governance” refers to the rules and procedures an organization establishes for AI workflows and how they interact with organizational data. Auditing is the process of assessing and validating systems to ensure safety, fairness, transparency, and legal compliance.

Technology leads and systems engineers are responsible for adhering to a structured set of guidelines for standards and processes usually issued by a governing body such as the European Union, the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, and the International Organization for Standardization.

The regulations aim to mitigate issues such as systemic bias, security vulnerabilities, and transparency risks, but they also highlight a critical skills gap.

Most traditional computer science, software, and electrical engineering degree programs were built around technical design and system architecture. They do not yet include training in AI auditing, data tracking, or safety protocols for how AI systems interact with people and other technologies.

Expecting mid-career engineers to leave their job to attend a full-time two- or four-year program to learn about the topics is not feasible. Yet treating safety and governance as an afterthought can lead to costly product delays, legal exposure, and broken public trust.

Targeted microcredential programs can bridge the knowledge gap by helping engineers build skills in compliance, AI ethics, and governance.

Skills-based microcredentials represent the mastery of expertise gained through a learning program. To earn them, learners must demonstrate the skill through a validation assessment. The microcredentials can be stacked, showing a growing skill set in a defined area and allowing learners to earn several microcredentials in one program.

Microcredentials also allow engineers to upskill and master critical competencies, such as bias mitigation, algorithmic transparency, and risk auditing, without interrupting their career. Through rigorous skills-validation assessments, microcredentials give tech leaders verifiable proof that their teams can audit systems effectively before deployment.

For engineering organizations, microcredentialing creates an agile upskilling pathway. It connects software engineering and hardware design directly to regulatory frameworks, empowering teams to certify systems for safety and compliance within their development life cycles.

Bridging technical capability and ethical responsibility requires a trusted foundation. IEEE has long been a pioneer in socio-technical standards, most notably through the IEEE 7000 series for ethics in AI system design, a framework created to address ethical considerations during the development life cycle.

The IEEE Credentialing Program translates the organization’s world-class standards into actionable, industry-aligned microcredentials. For more than three decades, IEEE has set the gold standard for technical validation and professional certification. By pairing cutting-edge AI governance standards with targeted microcredential programs, IEEE provides engineers and IT leaders with clear, standardized road maps to build systems that are not just technically advanced but also safe, compliant, and worthy of public trust.

To learn more about the credentialing program, explore the offerings or connect with an IEEE expert.

Kaitlyn Ridel is a marketing specialist for the IEEE Microcredentialing Program

#3257. ‘Much Ado About Nothing’ Broadway Review: Tom Hiddleston, Hayley Atwell & Jamie Lloyd Throw An Irresistible Party Of Shakespeare’s Great Comedy

Outside of ticker tape parades and New Year’s Eve in Times Square, you might be hard-pressed to think of a better, more joyous use of floating paper than the confetti that piles up nightly on the stage of Broadway‘s Winter Garden Theatre these days. We’re talking blizzards of the pink stuff, so deep that the man known for playing that Marvel trickster Loki can all but bury his superhero frame in the drifts.

The new, infectious Much Ado About Nothing, Jamie Lloyd‘s inventive and joyous revival of the Shakespeare comedy opening tonight at the Winter Garden, turns those old falling drifts of thin paper into a special effect that, for sheer exuberance, more than holds its own against the cutting-edge projections and awesome digital flimflammery delighting audiences at any number of Broadway houses this season. Related Stories News Josh Radnor & Beth Behrs To Join Broadway's 'Schmigadoon!' News Jonathan Spector's Acclaimed 'Birthright' Sets Spring Broadway Opening

Of course, even a confetti squall such as this wouldn’t impress a lick if the rest of Lloyd’s production couldn’t match its energy, and fortunately for us all this Much Ado About Nothing never lacks for giddy enchantment, from the Tony-worthy performances of stars Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell to the irresistible choreography of Fabian Aloise that will likely leave audiences of this straight play convinced they’ve just witnessed one of the best new musicals on Broadway this season. Watch on Deadline

Hiddleston, with his charm level cranked, and Atwell, best known to moviegoers for her Agent Carter of Marvel fame and here matching her fellow superhero beat for beat, play Benedick and Beatrice, two of Shakespeare’s most delightful characters, Loki-level tricksters who, as another character notes, engage in a “merry war” of plotting, planning and scheming in the name of love (though neither would admit to that motive, at least early on).

Lloyd, whose typically stark theatrical approach if on full view here but utilized to an effect wholly different than the shadows-and-light desolation of his A Doll’s House (starring Jessica Chastain) or Betrayal (which also paired him with Hiddleston), fashions this foray into Shakespeare as a 1990s-era dance club – at one point, the entire cast dons oversized, mascot-style headpieces (a chick, an octopus, a dog, a robot and more) suggesting so many ecstasy-fueled club kids packed into the Limelight.

The plot, of course, is the usual Shakespearean farce full of disguised identities, battles of the sexes, intricate schemes and star-crossed romances both helped and hindered by busybodies, eavesdroppers and nefarious in-laws. (In Shakespeare’s day, the word “nothing” carried a double meaning: In addition to our understood definition, “nothing” in its ye olde pronunciation carried a near-pun on the word “noting,” or gossip).

While productions of Shakespeare have long been interpreted with any number of contemporary spins and modern touches – such are the stock in trade of New York’s Shakespeare in the Park – Lloyd has come up with an approach that feels entirely fresh: Hiddleston, Atwell, the wonderful Mason Alexander Park and the rest of the cast move and sing to such jubilant dance and pop hits as Taylor Dayne’s “Tell It to My Heart,” C & C Music Factory’s “Gonna Make You Sweat (Everybody Dance Now),” Deee-Lite’s “Groove Is in the Heart,” and All-4-One’s “I Swear.” I knew we were in for a treat when Hiddleston’s Benedick and his boy crew made an entrance dancing to the Beastie Boys’ booming “Fight for Your Right (To Party).”

If period drama set to a more-or-less contemporary soundtrack doesn’t sound all that innovative – Six and Moulin Rouge! would like a word – Lloyd and his crack creative team (and his cast, of course) see to it that we pretty much forget all other contenders. With that ever-present pink confetti, a giant inflatable heart, character-accentuating modern dress (Soutra Gilmour did both the scenic design and the party-wear costume designs) and Jon Clark’s gorgeous lighting combine to create a dazzling experience. Like any dance club worth its cover charge, the sound design (by Ben and Max Ringham) is practically a showstopper in itself, with music thumping when it needs to thump and, when we need to hear dialogue, dropping to the sort of low-level thrum you might hear on the curb outside a packed club.

Hiddleston, whose last team-up with Lloyd was the austere Betrayal, is a revelation here, adding some incredibly hot dance moves to his overflowing bag of tricks. And he’s very, very funny (watch how he ever so deadpan blows a bit of stray confetti from his lips), playing off his movie star appeal with every sidelong glance and knowing grin seemingly directed to each person in the audience (he’s not above a quick show of gratitude when his seated admirers whoop their appreciation, as if his Benedick is welcoming everyone into his scheming maneuvers).

Atwell is every bit his equal, with Beatrice’s fiery, feminist mettle rendered as the true heart and brains of this tale. Both actor and role are this productions not-so-secret weapons – and yes, Lloyd and his cast are entirely in on the Marvel appeal going on here, so much so that Hiddleston-as-Loki and Atwell-as-Carter make brief appearances in the form of standees that had the audience at the reviewed performance all but levitating.

As good as they are – and they are – newcomer (to American audiences anyway) Mason Alexander Park as the sharp-tongued Margaret nearly walks off with the show, never more so than when, mic in hand, she/they performs “Tell It To My Heart” as if placing a dance-pop diva in 16th Century Milan is no more strange than wooing your heart’s desire.

Indeed, there’s no weak link in this cast, with James Phoon’s callow young Claudio swoon-worthy when he needs to be, infuriating when he’s a jerk; Tim Steed’s meddlesome Don John a hissable villain; and Gerald Kyd’s Don Pedro – that fair-weather father to the slandered Hero (a winning Mara Huf) – an appropriately garrulous, welcoming host (until he isn’t).

The grand appeal of this production is evident in just how much Hiddleston, Atwell and their compatriots seem to be enjoying themselves, and why not? So is everyone within the clarion-call-to-groove of those thumping, galvanizing dance beats.

Title: Much Ado About NothingVenue: Broadway’s Winter Garden TheatreWritten By: Willliam ShakespeareDirected By: Jamie LloydCast: Tom Hiddleston, Hayley Atwell, Mara Huf, Mika Onyx Johnson, Gerald Kyd, Forbes Masson, Phillip Olagoke, Mason Alexander Park, James Phoon, Tim SteedRunning Time: 2 hr 20 min (including intermission)

#3256. Apple among the companies facing pressure from US senators over ‘nudify’ apps [U: Apple, TTP respond]

The Guardian reports that three US senators have sent letters to the CEOs of Apple, Google, and Meta, demanding answers about their failure to prevent access to AI-powered ‘nudify’ apps. Here are the details.

Last month, Apple updated its App Store rules in an attempt to crack down on apps that enable users to generate nonconsensual nude images.

According to the updated rules, apps that allow users to create AI-generated content must include safeguards against abuse, including tools to filter objectionable material, report offensive content, and block abusive users.

Apple also warns that apps used primarily for pornographic content or the objectification of real people may be removed from the App Store without notice.

While definitely well-intended, Apple’s changes came amid growing reports of AI-powered nudify apps, which easily allow users to generate nonconsensual intimate images.

Two months before these changes, Apple removed an app that allowed users to create pornographic deepfakes of real people after WIRED reached out for comment, which in turn came one month after San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu demanded that Apple and Google remove several nudify apps from their app stores.

Apple also removed several apps following investigations by the Tech Transparency Project (TTP), which published reports in January and April revealing that such apps were widely available on the App Store, sometimes even appearing in sponsored search results.

Throughout these investigations, Apple has maintained that nudify apps have always been prohibited under its App Review Guidelines, and that it proactively rejects and removes apps that violate its policies, including those flagged through user reports.

Apple, of course, is not alone in this challenge, with Google facing similar criticism over their availability on the Play Store, and Meta coming under scrutiny for allowing developers to advertise these apps on Facebook and Instagram, as highlighted in the WIRED report mentioned above.

Which brings us to today’s report from The Guardian.

According to The Guardian’s exclusive report, “three Senate Democrats sent letters to tech CEOs saying safeguards against nudification apps are insufficient on their platforms.”

A trio of US Senators say Apple and Google are failing to effectively detect and remove apps that can be used to generate nonconsensual nude or pornographic imagery. They also say Meta is continuing to profit off of ads for these so-called nudification apps that “victimize women and girls worldwide”.

The senators, namely Ron Wyden of Oregon, Ed Markey of Massachusetts, and Ben Luján of New Mexico, claim that in addition to failing to remove these apps, the companies may actually be profiting from their distribution and promotion.

Commenting on the letter, both Google and Meta said they prohibit such apps or their promotion and work to detect and remove violations from their platforms, broadly echoing what Apple has repeatedly stated when reached for comment in the past over these same issues.

However, Wyden’s office argues that simply reaffirming, or in Apple’s case, updating these policies, means little if the companies continue to struggle to enforce them.

Keith Chu, the chief communications adviser and deputy policy director to Wyden, said that clarifying policies is not the same thing as enforcing them. Despite the companies reaffirming the prohibition of these apps, they continue to proliferate across Apple and Google app stores or be promoted in ads on Meta platforms, he added.

In its latest investigation, published just last month, TTP found 135 apps capable of generating nude or pornographic imagery on the App Store and the Play Store, using accounts registered to 13-year-old boys.

Additionally, researchers found that even accounts configured with parental controls were able to download these apps without requiring parental approval.

Despite Apple and Google removing the apps identified in the investigation, The Guardian noted that these apps continued to work on devices where they had already been installed.

Now, Senator Wyden warns that Congress may need to step in if the companies fail to do a better job of cracking down on these apps.

To read The Guardian’s full report, follow this link.

Update, 8:40 p.m. ET: In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple said:

“We designed the App Store to be a safe and trusted place for users. A number of the apps in the TTP report are mainstream photo and video editing tools with legitimate, widely used functionality, and do not have nudification or deepfake capabilities. We prohibit nudify apps on the App Store, and remove developers who add capabilities like it after the App Review process — a malicious tactic known as bait-and-switch. We previously removed 28 of the apps referenced in this report before it was shared with us and have taken action on the remaining apps found to violate our rules. The report also relies on testing from older software that does not reflect current Apple safety features, including expanded protections for teens and parental controls in Screen Time that give families the ability to block kids and teens from downloading apps rated above their age.”

Expanding on the safety features mentioned in its statement, Apple noted that teens aged 13 through 17 now have certain protections enabled by default, including web content filters, even if their parents haven’t configured any restrictions, and pointed to ⁠this support article for more information.

The company added that children under 13 are required to use Child Accounts, and that the report relied on its previous 17+ age rating system, which was replaced last year with a more granular system that includes 13+, 16+, and 18+ ratings.

Just curious. Why doesn't someone from Apple try out the app before approving it, rather than approving it and waiting until people complain? I know there are many thousands of apps on the App store. But given that Apple makes money off most of these apps, it could surely afford to hire a staff charged with reviewing submitted apps to ensure compliance with the App store's guidelines and requirements before making them available in the App store. What am I missing here?

Apple also noted that in its report, TTP counted apps depicting people in swimwear or lingerie, which the company said does not constitute nudification or, in itself, violate its guidelines.

As for parental controls, Apple explained that, although apps that exceed a child’s configured age restrictions won’t appear in curated App Store sections, they can still be found through search, allowing children to request permission to download them through Ask to Buy. Without parental approval, the download remains blocked.

Apple added that Ask to Buy is supposed to require parental approval even for purchases made using gift card balances, including subscriptions. The company said that if a purchase didn’t trigger an approval request, that would be unexpected behavior, and that it is investigating further.

Update, November 19, 4:00 p.m. ET: In response to Apple’s statement, TTP director Katie Paul reached out to 9to5Mac with the following comment:

Apple’s statement on nudify apps sidesteps important issues and leaves out key context. The company says it prohibits nudify apps but doesn’t address how its age rating system for apps contributes to the problem. TTP has shown how Apple relies on information provided by app developers to set age ratings—a self-reporting system that allows many nudify and pornographic apps to be misleadingly labeled a suitable for minors. Apple also continues to talk about removing nudify apps from the App Store, without mentioning that apps that are “removed” continue to be fully functional on people’s phones.

There are many questions about Apple’s policy on nudify apps that the statement fails to address. Apple has adopted a limited definition of “nudify.” The company defines nudify apps as capable of showing someone naked, not stripping them down to a bikini or lingerie. But the company also says it bans “creepy” and “nonconsensual intimate imagery.” What if an app is used to depict a woman in a bikini without her consent? We have asked Apple to clarify that and have not heard back.

As for Apple’s comment that TTP relied on “older software,” that may refer to the fact that Apple rolled out new child safety features in the fall. Our research was conducted in summer 2026. But many of Apple’s new features pertain to parent-supervised accounts on Apple, which have to be set up by a parent. Apple relies entirely on parents to go out of their way to locate and enable these settings. This raises obvious questions about how many people actually do this.

#3254. Instagram finally lets users edit Stories after publishing, but there’s a catch

Every once in a while, Instagram rolls out an update that addresses one of its users’ most longstanding requests. Today is one of those days.

As spotted by The Verge, Instagram head Adam Mosseri confirmed today that the app will finally let users edit a Story after publishing.

This means users will be able to add stickers and drawings, fix typos or adjust text, and even change the music without having to delete the Story and publish it again, which would mean losing any views it had already received.

The catch is that users will only have 15 minutes after publishing a Story to make changes by tapping the ellipsis button at the bottom of the screen, and then selecting “Edit story.”

Here’s Mosseri’s post announcing the news:

Today’s update is the latest in a series of changes Instagram has made this year to address longstanding user requests.

Back in March, the app introduced the ability to reorder photos and videos in a carousel after publishing. In April, it added an option to edit comments (also within 15 minutes of posting), and in June, it began letting users manually rearrange posts on their profile grid.

More recently, Instagram also brought its free Edits video editor to the Mac, with multi-track editing, advanced color grading tools, and 4K exports.

#3252. 28 Zero-Day Findings in Under Two Days. Is Robotics Security Keeping Pace?

VicOne’s AI-assisted research reveals what faster zero-day discovery means for robot safety

VicOne is a Physical AI cybersecurity company protecting vehicles and robots from cyber threats that can alter behavior and compromise safety.

VicOne used AI to find 28 zero-day vulnerabilities in Physical AI tools —these weaknesses can impact robot training, testing, and real-world control.

This article is brought to you by VicOne.

VicOne identified an initial set of 28 zero-day findings in less than two days using AI-assisted research across software and tools supporting the Physical AI ecosystem. These include projects developed or maintained by Google, NVIDIA, and Meta, among others.

Based on initial validation, all 28 findings are classified as zero-day vulnerabilities. The count may change following vendor and vulnerability-authority review, and some findings do not yet have CVE tracking numbers.

Many of these tools help teams train, simulate, test, and operate robots. Weaknesses in them could influence the models teams build, the test results they trust, and the instructions sent to robots.

These findings create two demands for robotics teams: responding as AI helps uncover weaknesses faster, and assessing how each one could affect robot safety and operations.

Vulnerability discovery involves examining code, tracing how systems communicate, and testing whether a suspected weakness can actually be exploited. AI can accelerate parts of this work, helping researchers analyze more software in less time. Attackers could use similar capabilities.

When the weakness is a zero-day — previously unknown and without an available fix — faster discovery can leave teams with little time to respond. While that exposure does not necessarily mean an attack has occurred, teams still need to determine whether they use the affected software and what an attacker could access or change.

VicOne’s findings span three stages of the robotics lifecycle: development and training, simulation and validation, and deployment and runtime. Weaknesses at each stage could affect what a robot learns, how it is tested, and how it is controlled.

Figure 1. In this research set, 75% of findings involved development, training, simulation, or validation tools, highlighting risks that can arise before a robot is deployed.VicOne

The following scenarios show how a compromised component could influence the robot at each stage.

These are potential consequences and not demonstrated outcomes for every finding. Actual effects depend on the attacker’s access, the system’s design, and whether other safeguards prevent the changes from reaching physical behavior.

In a separate demonstration, VicOne researchers provide a concrete example of a weakness affecting a protective function. The researchers exploited a vulnerability to prevent a robot’s remote-stop command from working. The case shows why teams need to test whether safeguards remain effective when the software supporting them is compromised.

Video 1. VicOne researchers demonstrate a vulnerability that prevents a robot’s remote-stop command from working. VicOne

AI can shorten the search for weaknesses, but a robotics team still needs to determine whether a fix is safe to deploy. Even after a software maintainer releases a patch, teams must identify affected systems, check compatibility, and verify that the update preserves intended behavior.

An earlier successful test remains useful evidence. However, a newly discovered weakness may reveal conditions that test never examined.

When immediate updating is impractical, teams may need temporary safeguards, such as restricting access to an affected service, while a validated fix is prepared.

As details from the 28 findings become available through coordinated disclosure, the next step is for robotics manufacturers is to connect each finding to its potential effect on development, deployment, and robot behavior.

That work also requires understanding how threats could affect robot behavior and how to protect systems already in operation. VicOne Radeis helps teams identify potential zero-day vulnerabilities, assess AI model and system security, and use simulation to evaluate how these risks could affect robot behavior before deployment. VicOne Rthena supports threat detection and responses within approved policies during operation.

Figure 2. Cybersecurity strengthens robot safety evidence throughout the lifecycle. VicOne helps teams test safety limits against manipulation before deployment and monitor the conditions behind safe behavior in operation.VicOne

Faster vulnerability discovery matters when teams can turn findings into action: identify what needs attention, verify that safeguards still hold, and confirm that a fix does not introduce new risks. That is how cybersecurity strengthens robot safety as systems continue to change.

For a deeper look how cybersecurity can affect robot safety, download our white paper, “Why Robot Safety Depends on Cybersecurity: Protecting the Information That Safety Decisions Rely On.”

VicOne is a Physical AI cybersecurity company protecting vehicles and robots from cyber threats that can alter behavior and compromise safety. Headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, the company provides automotive and robotics organizations with software and services to identify cyber risks early, assess their potential safety impact, and protect systems in operation, helping maintain safe, reliable behavior across real-world deployments.

#3251. Jennifer Love Hewitt “Had Not Seen” Ryan Phillippe Since ‘IKWYDLS’ When Reuniting For ‘9-1-1’ Crossover: “He Hadn’t Changed At All”

Nearly 30 summers later, Jennifer Love Hewitt recently had an onscreen reunion with Ryan Phillippe, courtesy of an upcoming 9-1-1 crossover.

The actress, who plays 9-1-1 dispatcher Maddie Kendall in the ABC flagship series, noted that before reuniting in the crossover with 9-1-1: Nashville, she and Phillippe had “not seen each other” since starring together in the 1997 teen slasher I Know What You Did Last Summer.

“We’ve been having the best time,” Hewitt told People after they teased their reunion in an Instagram video.

Noting that it was “so great” getting to reunite with Freddie Prinze Jr. as their IKWYDLS characters Julie James and Ray Bronson in last year’s legacy sequel, Hewitt explained that working with Phillippe on 9-1-1 “was very different” as he is “new in that universe,” recently joining 9-1-1: Nashville in Season 2 as New York detective Rogue Kelly. Watch on Deadline

“I’ve been in this universe for a while,” said Hewitt, who has played Maddie since Season 2 of 9-1-1 in 2018. “It’s such a safe, lovely place to be with the best people. And he and I have not seen each other since I was 18 years old.”

Having “never seen each other again” after wrapping the film, Hewitt noted that working together again “was a dream” and Phillippe “hadn’t — for me — changed at all,” adding that “he was the same in the most beautiful way.”

“And it was great. When we did the first movie together, his character was so terrible to me in that movie and hated me, but he was so lovely. … all I wanted to do was drink Joy Cola and like hang out with him because he had to be so mean to me [in the movie] that I just like wanted to be his friend. And he did it,” Hewitt added. “He held that space for me still, which was really beautiful.”

The upcoming 9-1-1 crossover with 9-1-1: Nashville comes amid the parent series’ 10th season and the spinoff’s sophomore season, airing back-to-back on Thursdays at 8/7c and 9/8c on ABC.

#3250. Zane Lowe shares Apple Music Radio audience numbers, recalls ‘crickets’ in the early days

In a new interview with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, Apple Music’s Zane Lowe discussed the early days of Apple Music Radio and revealed just how many people tune in each month. Here are the details.

Apple is rarely terribly specific about how many people use its services, including how many tune in to its radio stations.

In 2019, for instance, Eddy Cue said Beats 1 (now Apple Music 1) had ‘tens of millions of listeners,’ but Apple has rarely provided more specific figures since.

Apple Music’s Zane Lowe, however, has now offered a more concrete figure, revealing that the service reaches over 50 million unique listeners every month:

We were never, you know, delusional enough to assume we were going to get a huge audience overnight. We’d have to build it like anyone else would have to build anything. But we’ve just got to a point in our 11 years on where we now, overall, reach over 50 million unique listeners a month, which is a really large number for us, and it’s growing exponentially and really fast.

The revelation came in a wide-ranging interview published today with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, where Lowe discussed Apple Music Radio’s early struggles, its approach to supporting emerging artists, and why human curation remains central to the service.

When discussing the early days at Apple Music, Lowe recalled:

When we started the radio here, I didn’t have access or opportunity with a lot of the artists that I built relationships with from the BBC because we were unproven. And I came over here thinking, “Well, I’ve got Jimmy Iovine over here, and I’ve got Apple over here and I feel unstoppable, and who’s not going to want to come and launch this thing with us?” But it was kind of crickets… As upsetting as that was at the time, two good things came out of it. Number one, it snapped me back into the reality force field of building something from scratch. And number two, it made us focus really clearly and in a big way on new and emerging artists.

He also mentioned some of the first artists Apple Music Radio supported, including Billie Eilish with “Ocean Eyes,” Khalid with American Teen, and Bryson Tiller with his first song.

At the time, Lowe noted, these artists were just getting started, and supporting emerging talent became a defining part of Apple Music Radio’s approach, one that continues to this day:

The really cool number is on our radio network. We played — this year alone — over 6,500 individual artists, which is not a commercial radio model. [Other radio networks’] playlists are very small, and the amount of plays is very great. Our playlist is gigantic. We play a lot of different artists, and over half of those 6,500 artists we’ve played in one year are new or emerging. So, think about 3,300 artists, roughly, getting played, who may be on their first song, their first EP, their first album…It’s proof of concept. It’s great.

Still on the subject of the early days at Apple Music, Lowe said “it was very clear [from the start] that that was very important to everybody who was responsible for bringing Apple Music to life,” adding that “serving artists and the artistic community in a way that is of most value and of most service” still drives “a lot of the decision-making” at the platform.

When the conversation turned to Apple Music’s recent rebranding, which introduced a new logo physically created using sound waves from a composition by Fred again.., Lowe said he couldn’t speak to the decisions behind it, but stressed the human element and the creative process that went into it:

We could have created that in a way that could utilize all of the tech available. We could type that into a prompt. But at the end of the day, seeing how it’s made is so much more additionally inspiring than just seeing it. It speaks to, I think, what we try to do here, which is, we love the process of what we do, and the result is a byproduct of getting to do it and loving to do it.

The issue of algorithms also came up when Lowe discussed Apple Music’s approach to music discovery, with the executive emphasizing the importance of human curation over automated recommendations:

Well, we don’t want to say that too loudly, because someone could be like, “Wait a minute, we could cut costs here? Man, how did we not think of that!” Look, I mean, jokes aside, we’ve been incredibly fortunate, and I’ve been incredibly fortunate to take that step from the BBC into a company and to work with people that value exactly what it is you’re describing: this idea of place and this experience of sharing things with each other, and how meaningful it is when someone shares a record with you and it comes with context. It’s a gift…

#3246. ‘Sunrise On The Reaping’ Epilogue Scene Explained: How Everything Ties Together

SPOILER ALERT: This post spoils the end of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

The epilogue scene at the end of The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping echoes the chapter that closes Suzanne Collins’ novel of the same name.

Woody Harrelson, Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson appear in the final moment of the film, reprising their roles of Haymitch Abernathy, Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark, respectively, from The Hunger Games (2012), The Hunger Games: Catching Fire (2013), The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 1 (2014) and The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 2 (2015).

It was known that Lawrence and Hutcherson would return for the second prequel film. Harrelson could have been a given once they were confirmed, since his character centers the latest movie. In The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, which tells the villain origin story of Coriolanus Snow (Tom Blyth), Donald Sutherland’s voice was used in the end to tie the first prequel film to the original four, in which Sutherland portrayed the poisonous president. Watch on Deadline

The Sunrise scene in particular is meaningful with these three actors behind their roles because it connects the past and present, bridging the gap between The Sunrise on the Reaping and Suzanne Collins’ original trilogy of books plus their film adaptations. Haymitch, in his Quarter Quell Hunger Games, did so much to advance the rebellion that would eventually bring down Panem, the Capitol and the barbaric tradition that killed children ever year. It was Katniss who ultimately gained the momentum from this spark — symbolized by Haymitch’s flint striker and more — to topple the dystopian society and cruel reign of President Snow (Ralph Fiennes in Sunrise on the Reaping and Donald Sutherland in the first four films).

Katniss and Peeta wish Haymitch a happy birthday in the ending scene, symbolizing that he did, in fact, reach a birthday where the sun didn’t rise on another reaping ceremony, which was his love Lenore Dove’s (Whitney Peak) dying wish. It took another 25 years after his games, which doubled the amount of tributes entered as is custom for a Quarter Quell, to overcome the tyranny. The 50th Hunger Games added a wrinkle, or extra rule, to make those games extra gruesome.

By then, Peeta and Katniss, who had already somewhat thwarted the Gamemakers by threatening to each eat poisonous nightlock berries and die for there to be no victor in their 74th games, experienced a terrible Quarter Quell of their own. The 75th Hunger Games — or third Quarter Quell — involved the wrinkle that each pair of district tributes would be reaped from their existing pool of victors.

The Catching Fire film made it seem like Plutarch Heavensbee (Philip Seymour Hoffman) and President Snow (Donald Sutherland) devised that wrinkle themselves to particularly torture Katniss and send her a message about her sedition. In the books, the founders of Panem left a box behind that laid out the rules of each Quarter Quell game, making it seem more like coincidence that this happened when a full-blown rebellion was close at hand.

While preparing for the third Quarter Quell, Katniss and Peeta leaned on Haymitch for his experience in the games in addition to meeting other victors turned mentors turned tributes once more like Mags (Lynn Cohen), Beetee (Jeffrey Wright), Wiress (Amanda Plummer) and others, younger versions of whom played roles in Haymitch’s story before the big Catching Fire revolt as well.

“The seeds of Haymitch Abernathy’s backstory were planted over twenty years ago when I began the original trilogy,” author Suzanne Collins wrote in a letter timed to the film’s release. “In Catching Fire, Katniss and Peeta watch the recap of his Second Quarter Quell games as he silently observes from the shadows. The Capitol had warped the true account and spun reality into vicious propaganda. For Haymitch to tell the truth about what happened would’ve been too dangerous for his tributes and too traumatic for him.”

At the end of the snippet, Haymitch goes to the meadow to feed his flock of geese, which he raises in memory of Lenore Dove, but not before Katniss and Peeta thank him, and he in return thanks them for their teamwork in dismantling the dictatorship they lived under for so long.

As for whether there could be more films in the franchise, it seems like it would come down to Collins and her decision to write another book or two. Fans have been particularly vocal about wanting more of one Finnick Odair’s first Hunger Games, and director Francis Lawrence as well as star Joseph Zada have expressed interest in diving into Plutarch’s (Jesse Plemons) story as well as the lore behind the mysterious District 13, which makes itself known in the Mockingjay books and films. Collins is known for writing these books only when she has something to say and express through them. The final scene at the end of Sunrise on the Reaping could make a great close to the story as is.

#3245. Advanced Metrology for Defect Detection, Tool Health, and Semiconductor Yield Enhancement



In advanced semiconductor manufacturing, small defects can have a large effect on yield. Thin film deposition tools must stay stable and qualified. Process drift must be caught early. When a defect does appear, engineers need to know where it came from and how it affects device performance. This webinar shows how in-line inspection and offline characterization combine into one workflow, from tool monitoring to root-cause analysis.

In the first half, Dr. Bitan Chakraborty from Intel, explains how surface scan metrology fits into station monitors for thin film tools. The session shows how baseline signatures and real-time monitoring reveal hardware wear, particle generation, and process drift before they reach production wafers. It then moves to in-line scans on patterned wafers. These scans expose layer-level defects and show how they form and spread through multi-layer device stacks. Linking this defect data to electrical test results helps teams find root causes and focus their yield improvement work.

In the second half, Dr. Jacob Petersen from Evident Scientific, addresses a common question: what happens after an in-line tool flags a problem? In-line tools are fast, but they cannot always provide the details needed for a firm conclusion. Offline 3D optical profilometry fills that gap by combining three complementary inspection techniques in a single system. It delivers dimensional measurements and helps determine whether a defect lies within the sample or comes from foreign material. The session covers how several optical techniques support inspection from bare silicon to fully packaged chips. It also shows how automation enables fast measurement of features down to the sub-nanometer scale with minimal operator handling.

What You Will Learn:

  • How surface scan metrology in station monitors tracks tool health and supports the qualification of thin film deposition processes
  • How baseline signatures and real-time monitoring detect particle generation, hardware degradation, and process drift before production is affected
  • How in-line scans on patterned wafers reveal layer-level defects and show how they propagate through multi-layer device structures
  • When offline 3D optical profilometry should follow in-line inspection, and how it measures dimensions and separates sample defects from foreign material
  • How correlating tool health data, inspection results, and electrical performance links physical defects to yield loss and guides targeted improvement projects
